### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **5** package(s): `@objectstack/core`, `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, `@objectstack/objectql`, `@objectstack/plugin-hono-server`, `@objectstack/plugin-security`, touching **23** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/core/src/security/index.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**17** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json ff88105061012c8b14f7ec937d7b3113e404e922`.

⛔ **8** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/core/src/security/index.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- the SDK route bridge reached **60** of **216** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **156** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **156**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **101** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **61** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json ff88105061012c8b14f7ec937d7b3113e404e922` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `74fc7b4d305b168d7c329958d009a8022d42172f` — the merge of head `0a0e00229cd391adb51908655bf967c0008bef4b` into base `ff88105061012c8b14f7ec937d7b3113e404e922`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 74fc7b4d305b168d7c329958d009a8022d42172f && git checkout 74fc7b4d305b168d7c329958d009a8022d42172f
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin ff88105061012c8b14f7ec937d7b3113e404e922 0a0e00229cd391adb51908655bf967c0008bef4b && git checkout -B drift-repro ff88105061012c8b14f7ec937d7b3113e404e922 && git merge --no-ff 0a0e00229cd391adb51908655bf967c0008bef4b

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json ff88105061012c8b14f7ec937d7b3113e404e922
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs ff88105061012c8b14f7ec937d7b3113e404e922` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

### ① Derived judgments

**Row 1 — `/auth/me/permissions` leaves out a disabled package's objects. RIGHT.**

- One predicate, no second spelling. `registryObjectPackageDisabled(registry)` calls `registry.isObjectPackageDisabled(name)` on the registry itself. The data plane's refusal (`assertObjectRegistered` → `isObjectOfDisabledPackage` in `protocol.ts`) calls the same method. `SchemaRegistry.isObjectPackageDisabled` resolves the name through `resolveObjectKey` and asks the OWNER's package (`#7557`), so the map leaves out exactly the objects `/data/<object>` refuses `404 OBJECT_PACKAGE_DISABLED`. The objectql pin asserts both halves on one harness (`assertObjectRegistered` throws the code; the map has no entry).
- Byte-identical doors. The only two production builders of the map are `plugin-hono-server` (`/auth/me/permissions`) and `plugin-security` (`ISecurityService.getEffectiveObjectPermissions`); both hand `isObjectPackageDisabled: registryObjectPackageDisabled(ql?.registry)`. The engine's `current_user.can()` resolver seam is registered by the security plugin with that same method (`registerEffectiveObjectPermissionsResolver`), so the console, the server's `visibleWhen`/`formula`/`defaultValue` evaluation and the write wall read one map. The hono and security pins assert `JSON.stringify` equality with the core function; the security pin evaluates `current_user.can('deal','read')` through `ExpressionEngine` and gets `false` for an admin (super-user seed) and a member (explicit grant). The hono route's `catch` answers the closed shape and needs no accessor.
- `can()` false: the omission runs LAST, over the explicit grant, the super-user seed and the wildcard's coverage; the `'*'` entry is kept (it is not an object, and `objectPermissionGrants` reads the object's own entry). Pinned per source in core and for read/create/edit/delete in objectql.
- Re-enable without restart: core caches nothing; the security plugin memoises set resolution, not the map; the registry's `enablePackage` flips the record in place. Pinned in objectql, hono and security.
- No caller left out. `git grep buildEffectiveObjectPermissions` on the head: the two doors above and the tests; nothing builds the map without the accessor. Failure posture: a registry without the method disables nothing, and a throwing predicate warns and leaves the map whole (the same guard as the seed and the `apiOperations` annotation). That is fail-open to main's answer, display-only, since the data plane still refuses the object; it matches `isObjectOfDisabledPackage`'s optional-call posture and is acceptable.
- Not pruned, by the order's wording: the `fields` slot still carries `OBJECT.FIELD` entries of a disabled object. `can()` does not read it; the dev records it as a carrier-seat finding. Noted, not a defect of this PR.

**Row 2 — an action launching into a disabled package is withheld where #24400 withholds. RIGHT, with one acceptance-note correction (should-fix 1).**

- The seam is #24400's. `boundServedActions` replaced `isPackageDisabled(_packageId)` with `isActionWithheldByDisabledPackage(action)`, whose first arm is that same test, so #24400's rule is a strict subset. The three new arms: `objectName` object of a disabled package (see Premise correction), `type: 'flow'` target that only disabled packages ship (`isFlowOfDisabledPackage`), and a param `objectOverride` naming an object of a disabled package (`isObjectPackageDisabled`, the row-1 predicate). `hasDisabledPackage()` short-circuits the walk when nothing is disabled, so an enabled installation pays nothing and serves exactly what it served.
- Three served faces, one predicate: (a) the served object fold — `attachBoundActions` on the `'served'` layer filters the object's OWN `actions` (where `defineStack()` leaves a same-stack bound action) and attaches only `boundServedActions`; `registry.getObject` and the protocol's `getMetaItem({type:'object'})` both end there; (b) the protocol's effective served list — `readFlattenedMetaItems` filters only when `request.type === 'action' && audience === 'served' && servedOverride` (`layer: 'effective'`), which is what `GET /meta/action` calls; (c) the served by-name read — `readMetaItemFace` with `face === 'served'` answers a withheld action as a name with nothing behind it, as `isItemOfDisabledPackage` does. All three are pinned in one block on the real `ObjectQL` + protocol harness.
- Unchanged, and rightly: `getMetaItemsForExecution` / `getMetaItemForExecution` (audience `'execution'`), `getMetaItemsPerPackage` (`layer: 'per-package'`, `servedOverride` false — the package export), and the code layer (`attachBoundActions(..., 'code')`, `getArtifactItem`). The execution plane keeps the declaration so the ADR-0066 D4 gate, the activation ledger and the dispatch trichotomy still read it; the package export keeps what the package ships. Pinned ("the execution list and the code layer keep what each package ships").
- "Flow target only served by a disabled package": `isFlowOfDisabledPackage` answers true only when at least one flow of that name is registered AND every one is owned by a disabled package; a twin flow from an enabled package, a runtime-authored row with no `_packageId`, or a name the registry holds no flow for are not disabled. Right: the automation engine binds from the list, which omits only a disabled package's items, so a twin keeps the launch alive. Pinned including the twin registered AFTER the disable (which exercises the new `registerItem('flow')` invalidation).
- Cache invalidation is complete for the new verdict inputs: a flow registered or unregistered while any package is disabled, a package uninstall that removes `flow/` items, and the uninstall of a disabled package each `invalidateAll()`; disable/enable already did (#24400). A7 reddens exactly the twin-flow case.
- A withheld own-action still blocks an attached twin of its name (`present` is built from `base`, not `kept`): deliberate, so nothing stands in for a withheld action.

**Premise correction (the `objectName` arm). IN SCOPE as a bounded in-place fix, and declared.** The order says "withheld wherever #24400 withholds an action bound to a disabled package's object" on `GET /api/v1/meta/action`. The dev measured on the first head that #24400 withheld it only by hiding the object: the enabled package's action bound by `objectName` to the module's object was still listed and served by name (`listed= true byName= true object= OBJECT_PACKAGE_DISABLED`). The arm is one line on the same predicate, in the same files and gate families, pinned by `bound_to_member` in the `[#28877]` block, ablated A8 (reddens only that case, 46/47), and declared in the changeset's FROM (third bullet) and TO (objectql bullet) and in the PR body's Acceptance notes. Not scope creep: without it row 2's "wherever #24400 withholds" would be false on `/meta/action`. The seat records the premise correction on the card at hand-back.

**Row 3.** Not touched; answered by row 2 (the dialog is not reached once the action is withheld). The seat answers row 3 on the card.

**Caller classes.** Admin and member are both measured for row 1 (security pin: `ops_admin` seed, `sales` grant; objectql pin: wildcard and explicit grant). Row 2 reads no caller: the withholding is in the served metadata. Nothing that legitimately needs a disabled package loses access: the Packages page reads `GET /api/v1/packages` (the `package` type is never filtered) and `PATCH /packages/:id/enable` is gated on the `manage_metadata` system permission, not the object map; `/meta/object` already omitted the disabled objects before this PR. A system context gets the same omission, which is consistent: `assertObjectRegistered` refuses every caller. The dispatch door `POST /actions/OBJECT/ACTION` is unchanged in code; see should-fix 1 for its answer.

**Out of scope held.** No change to navigation, the disable door or the data-plane refusal.

**Evidence.** Red first: row 2 at BASE for the three row-2 files reddens exactly the "disabled" and twin-flow cases (2/47), row-1 files green; row 1 with the omission ablated reddens exactly the omission cases in all four packages, row-2 cases green. Ablations A3–A8 each redden only their own cases (A3 protocol filter: the list assertion only; A4 flow arm: "disabled" + twin; A5 override arm; A6 own-actions filter: the inline action; A7 flow-registration invalidation: the twin; A8 objectName arm). Controls: before-disable, re-enable, twin flow, execution list, code layer, `'*'` kept, the other package untouched. Full package suites green on `de04ea75`, the second commit re-run in its own files on `934a10f5` (47/47); typecheck exit 0 on all five. Full dogfood battery on `934a10f5` (narrowing arm): 382 files / 3156 tests passed, no failure. Gates: 71 derived, 70 exit 0, `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` NOT MEASURED locally (needs every `dist/`), left to CI's Build Core. Overlap: #28903 (app-shell PackagesPage, UI) and #28889 (closed, UI permissions provider) touch none of this diff's files.

**CI on the head at review time:** no red. Completed success: Check Changeset, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Dogfood Regression Gate, every Lint lane, Type Check · source gates and · debt ledger, Live E2E UI, PR-body guards, Check PR Size, Flag docs. Still in progress: Build Core (carries `dual-build-cjs-loads`), Test Core 1–8, Type Check · workspace and · consumer gates, Build & E2E UI, Test UI 1–16, Type Check UI. The landing precheck ② is the seat's read of the final check-runs.

### ② Semver level

**Declared:** `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` · `Metadata-protocol: narrowed` · `minor` on core, objectql, metadata-protocol, plugin-hono-server, plugin-security · BREAKING banner with FROM → TO · `<!-- adr-0087: not-required (no-migration-prescription) … -->`. PR body and changeset agree with each other, and the level follows the declared kind, so the gates are green.

**Judged:**

- `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` — RIGHT. The published surface widens (one optional member on `EffectiveObjectPermissionsSchemaSource`, `registryObjectPackageDisabled`, `isActionWithheldByDisabledPackage` on the registry and the protocol module) and two served answers narrow while a package is disabled. `yes` + the `(narrowing)` arm is the one legal spelling for widen+narrow.
- `Metadata-protocol: narrowed` — WRONG. The kind is "the change to what a metadata author can write": `narrowed` is a key removed or tombstoned, a value refused, a requirement tightened. Nothing an author writes is refused or tightened here: every object, flow, action, `type: 'flow'` target and `objectOverride` is accepted exactly as before, and the changeset's own ADR-0087 marker says so in terms ("no spec key, authorable spelling, export or stored shape is removed, renamed or re-shaped"). What narrows is two served answers under a runtime package state. That is a non-protocol narrowing, and ruling A on #25105 (`check-changeset-no-major.mjs`, its ruling block and self-test) says: "A non-protocol widening (REST) or narrowing (a driver, a posture) ships `patch` and keeps its BREAKING banner and its ADR-0087 disposition unchanged." The repo's precedent is exactly this shape: eleven changesets with `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` + `Metadata-protocol: none` at `patch` (the orgless-boot refusal, the CBP master boot refusal, the plugin-auth load refusal, the datasource-refused line in objectql, …), each banner saying "it changes what boots/serves, not what a metadata author can write, so it ships as `patch`".
- Consequence of the mis-declaration: `narrowed` is a breaking carrier of its own (signal 5 in the ADR-0087 gate) and the release-notes classifier files a `narrowed` bullet with a `not-required` disposition under "需手动处理 — action required: narrowed, with no ADR-0087 conversion", telling every reader of five packages' release notes that an authored key needs hand migration. None does. The five-package `minor` footprint follows the same error: under `none` every introduced entry is `patch`, and the level gate refuses a `minor` beside `none`, so the two lines and the five levels move together.
- `adr-0087: not-required (no-migration-prescription)` — RIGHT, and still required after the fix: the `(narrowing)` arm and the BREAKING banner each declare breaking, so a disposition is owed, and this category is the honest one (no migration prescription anywhere in the body; the gate validated it, exit 0 locally and Check Changeset green).
- Five packages, not one: right. Each of the five publishes a changed runtime (core: the function; objectql: the predicate and the fold; metadata-protocol: the list and by-name filters; the two plugins: the accessor handed over). After the fix, five `patch` entries.

**Must-fix M1 (changeset + PR body, no code):** in `.changeset/28877-disabled-package-grants-and-launch-actions.md` and the PR body, `Metadata-protocol: none`; all five frontmatter entries `patch`; the banner line reads "shipped as `patch`" (a served-answer narrowing, not what an author writes). Keep `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)`, the BREAKING banner, FROM → TO and the `adr-0087: not-required (no-migration-prescription)` marker unchanged.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions`: none from the dev.
- Dev-flagged, out-of-scope findings (carrier: the seat), both read and agreed: the `fields` slot still carries a disabled object's `OBJECT.FIELD` entries (harmless, `can()` reads `objects`); the dispatch door still answers its own 404. Neither needs a card now.
- **Should-fix S1 (PR body wording, no code):** the Acceptance note "the dispatch door … still answers the launch's own refusal (`404` "Flow … not found")" is true for a bound action that keeps a top-level copy (the execution by-name read finds it, `ownsRoute` admits it, the launch fails), but not for an action declared only inside the object (the test's `inline_enroll`): `resolveRouteActionDeclaration` reads `ql.getSchema` = `registry.getObject` = the served fold, misses the withheld embedded action, and the execution by-name read has no standalone item, so the answer is ADR-0110 D3's "no declaration" `404`. Fail-closed, nothing runs ungated, the console no longer draws the button; only the note's text is wrong.
- **Should-fix S2 (hand-back):** the seat records on the card the premise correction (#24400 hid a bound action only by hiding its object; the `objectName` arm closes it), answers row 3 as "answered by row 2", and notes the `fields` slot finding as carried.
